questions.q: Select the option that will correct the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no correction is required, select No correction needed.
o: No correction needed
questions.s:
Answer: c) No correction needed

Explanation:
The sentence "Naveen is as tall as Rocky." is grammatically correct.

  • "As tall as" is the correct structure for making an equal comparison between two people or things (दो चीज़ों या व्यक्तियों की बराबरी दिखाने के लिए)।
     e.g., She is as intelligent as her brother.
       Naveen is as tall as Rocky. ✅

Other options are incorrect:

  • "Taller than" = used for comparative degree when one is taller than the other (ऊँचाई में फर्क हो)

  • "Tall as" = incomplete structure, needs "as" before it

  • "The tallest" = superlative form used when comparing more than two

So, no correction is needed in this sentence.

questions.q: Change the following sentence into positive degree.
o: Yash is best than Harsh.
Yash is as good as Harsh.
Yash and Harsh both are good.
Yash is not good than Harsh.
questions.s:
Correct answer: Yash is as good as Harsh.

Explanation:

  • The sentence "Yash is not better than Harsh" means both have equal ability or quality.

  • The positive degree to express equality is "Yash is as good as Harsh."

  • Other options:

  • Yash is best than Harsh – incorrect comparative and superlative usage

  • Yash and Harsh both are good – correct in meaning but less direct

  • Yash is not good than Harsh – grammatically incorrect

Correct sentence:
"Yash is as good as Harsh."

questions.q: He couldn't attend the morning session, so he joined the later part of the workshop in the afternoon.
o: He couldn't attend the morning session
so he joined the later part
of the workshop in the afternoon.
questions.s:
The correct option is (b) "so he joined the later part."

"Later" refers to time, whereas "latter" refers to the second of two things mentioned. In this context, "latter" is more appropriate as it refers to the second part of the workshop, rather than a later time.

  • Since the sentence contrasts morning session with the afternoon part, "latter part" is more appropriate.

The corrected sentence would be: "He couldn't attend the morning session, so he joined the latter part of the workshop in the afternoon."
